Pearls are delicate, so the approach is simple: wipe with a dry cloth after each wear, and avoid anything harsh or wet.After wearing, use a dry polishing cloth to remove oils and pollutants. If your pearl piece has a metal setting you'd like to clean separately, you can carefully use a cotton swab dipped in rubbing alcohol on the band or earring posts, just avoid getting cleaner on the pearls themselves.Store pearls flat and separate from other jewelry in a soft, velvet-lined box to prevent scratching. Never submerge pearls in water or use ultrasonic or steam cleaners, as these damage both the gems and the stringing. Skip harsh chemicals like vinegar, ammonia, or bleach, and avoid wearing pearls while exercising, swimming, or doing housework. Pearls should be the last thing you put on and the first thing you take off, so they stay away from skin oils, lotions, cosmetics, and perfumes.For a more detailed guide, check out our full pearl care article.
turns.literal: What is the right way to clean pearls?
